Cameco reports third quarter results: year-to-date performance as expected;
nuclear industry fundamentals continue to strengthen; disciplined strategy and integrated nuclear exposure support long-term value creation; annual dividend declared
October 30, 2026
Cameco (TSX: CCO; NYSE:
CCJ) today reported its consolidated financial and operating results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS).
“We continue to be guided by our disciplined strategy and the strength of our diversified nuclear energy platform,” said Tim Gitzel,
Cameco’s CEO. “Results for the quarter and the first nine months of 2026 were lower than the comparable period last year, largely due to a few significant items that affected year-over-year comparisons. We planned a longer maintenance
outage at the Key Lake mill this year to undertake projects that are intended to ensure flexibility and sustainable operations, and as we expected, that outage, which began during the third quarter, resulted in lower production volume and higher
costs this quarter. Last year, Westinghouse also received a significant payment related to the Dukovany nuclear project in the Czech Republic, so our equity earnings from our investment in Westinghouse for the first nine months of 2026 were lower.
As with nearly every industry, we also continue to experience inflationary pressure, while broader market volatility is affecting sentiment. However, it is important to distinguish between changes in market sentiment and changes in underlying
fundamentals. In our view, the fundamentals supporting nuclear energy remain stronger than ever. The reactors operating around the world today continue to require fuel; we believe fuel-cycle capacity remains constrained in many parts of the western
market, and utilities continue to evaluate their long-term fuel requirements in an increasingly uncertain geopolitical environment. Importantly, our ownership interest in Westinghouse extends our participation across the nuclear value chain,
providing exposure to reactor services, operating reactors and future deployment opportunities.
“We are encouraged by the increasing level of
engagement we are seeing with customers as utilities continue to assess security of supply, fuel availability and future procurement needs. As we have consistently said, contracting activity is rarely linear and market conditions can influence the
pace of utility decision-making, but customer requirements do not disappear. We believe our contract portfolio continues to provide valuable insight into future demand and remains central to how we evaluate opportunities and inform supply and
investment decisions across our business.
“At Cameco, our strategy is built on discipline. We pursue disciplined contracting that supports
long-term value creation, we use those commitments to inform our supply decisions, and we maintain disciplined financial management when allocating capital. We will not advance production, commit capital or pursue growth simply in response to
headlines, short-term price movements or market enthusiasm surrounding any single theme. Instead, we remain focused on risk-adjusted returns, customer commitments and creating sustainable value for our owners over the long term.
“While growing electricity demand associated with artificial intelligence, data centres and the broader technology sector may provide additional upside
for nuclear energy, it is important to recognize that our investment thesis does not depend on any single demand driver. The existing reactor fleet, life extensions, restarts, committed new-build activity,
energy-security priorities and the need to replace declining supply continue to underpin our long-term outlook today. We believe our combination of proven assets, long-term customer relationships, supply flexibility and integrated exposure across
the nuclear value chain provides a resilient foundation through periods of market volatility, and the potential for meaningful upside as nuclear growth continues to unfold. Stronger fundamentals reinforce our confidence in the market and underscore
the importance of disciplined execution.”
- 1 -
Third Quarter Highlights
FINANCIAL HIGHLIGHTS

Consolidated performance: Third quarter results included net earnings of $43 million, adjusted net
loss of $2 million, and adjusted EBITDA of $267 million while results for the first nine months of the year included net earnings of $199 million, adjusted net earnings of $279 million and adjusted EBITDA of $1.2 billion.
Results for the quarter and first nine months of the year were generally lower than in 2025, primarily due to lower equity earnings from our investment in Westinghouse, as well as lower sales volumes and higher average unit cost of sales, partially
offset by higher average realized prices. See Consolidated financial results and Financial results by segment – Uranium in the third quarter MD&A for more information.

Strong balance sheet: Thanks to our risk-managed financial discipline, our balance sheet remains strong.
As of September 30, 2026, we had $860 million in cash and cash equivalents, $1.0 billion in total debt and a $1.0 billion undrawn revolving credit facility.

Dividend: Our board of directors declared a 2026 annual dividend of $0.24 per common share, payable on
December 15, 2026, to shareholders of record on November 30, 2026. The decision to declare an annual dividend is reviewed regularly by our board in the context of our cash flow, financial position, strategy and other relevant factors,
including appropriate alignment with the cyclical nature of our earnings.

Uranium : In our core uranium segment, third quarter earnings before taxes were $175 million and
adjusted EBITDA was $179 million compared to $172 million and $220 million, respectively, in 2025, due to our normal quarterly variations in deliveries and our lower planned 2026 sales delivery volumes resulting from our contracting
discipline. Earnings before taxes for the first nine months of the year were $703 million and adjusted EBITDA was $855 million, compared to $681 million and $862 million in 2025, respectively. See Financial results by segment
– Uranium in our third quarter MD&A for more information.

Fuel Services : In our Fuel Services segment, third quarter earnings before taxes were $13 million and
adjusted EBITDA was $24 million, compared to $17 million and $25 million in 2025, respectively. Earnings before taxes for the first nine months of the year were $87 million while adjusted EBITDA was $120 million, compared to
$129 million and $158 million in 2025, respectively, due to our normal variations in the mix of Fuel Services products sold. See Financial results by segment – Fuel services in our third quarter MD&A for more information.

Westinghouse : Westinghouse reported a net loss of $24 million (our share) for the third quarter, an
improvement from a net loss of $32 million (our share) in the third quarter of 2025. Over the first nine months of the year, Westinghouse reported a net loss of $80 million (our share), in comparison to net earnings of $32 million
(our share) in the same period in 2025. Equity earnings from our investment in Westinghouse were lower than in 2025 due to Westinghouse’s participation in the construction project for two nuclear reactors at the Dukovany power plant in the
Czech Republic, which resulted in an approximate US$170 million increase in our share of Westinghouse’s 2025 second quarter revenue. To better reflect the underlying operating performance, we use adjusted EBITDA as a performance measure
for Westinghouse. In the third quarter of 2026, our share of Westinghouse’s adjusted EBITDA was $143 million, compared to $124 million in the third quarter of 2025, while adjusted EBITDA for the first nine months was
$427 million, compared to $569 million in 2025. See Financial results by segment - Westinghouse , in our third quarter MD&A for more information.
Adjusted net earnings and adjusted EBITDA are non-IFRS measures. See page 5.
OPERATIONAL HIGHLIGHTS

Uranium: At the Key Lake mill, the annual maintenance shutdown began in the third quarter and included the
installation of new infrastructure and repairs to major existing infrastructure. As a result of the substantial work, the shutdown was planned to be longer than in previous years and commissioning of the new infrastructure is underway. As we
approach the end of the year, we have greater certainty in the timing of uranium production and deliveries. See Outlook for 2026 and Our operations in our third quarter MD&A for more information.

JV Inkai: JV Inkai remains on track to produce 10.4 million pounds of U 3 O 8 (100% basis) in 2026, of which our purchase allocation is expected to be 4.2 million pounds of U 3 O 8 . In the first nine months of the year, we purchased 0.8 million pounds of U 3 O 8 from JV Inkai and following the quarter, a shipment containing approximately 1.6 million pounds of our share of Inkai’s 2026 production was delivered to Blind River. The final shipment
of our remaining share of JV Inkai’s 2026 production is currently in transit and expected to arrive at Blind River prior to the end of 2026. See Our operations- Uranium 2026 Q3 Updates in our third quarter MD&A for more information.
- 2 -

Fuel Services: We continue to expect our annual production, which includes UF 6 conversion, UO 2 conversion and heavy water reactor fuel bundles, to be between 13 million and 14 million kgU. See Our
Operations - Fuel Services 2026 Q3 Updates in our third quarter MD&A for more information.

Westinghouse: In October, Westinghouse announced conditional purchase orders with four Polish suppliers to
support the build out of the Polskie Elektrownie Jadrowe’s project and the first AP1000 unit at the Lubiatowo-Kopalino site. Separately, Westinghouse was authorized to begin procuring long-lead nuclear components, helping secure critical
supply chain capacity, reduce project execution risk and support the planned development schedule. Also in October, Westinghouse launched a US State Department-funded FEED study for an AP1000 reactor at Slovakia’s Jaslovské Bohunice
site, advancing engineering, licensing and project planning for the proposed new nuclear plant, supporting the country’s energy security objectives.
MARKETING HIGHLIGHTS

Deliveries and inventory: In the third quarter, we delivered 5.6 million pounds of U 3 O 8 , which is consistent with our sales plan and reflects our normal quarterly delivery variations. With production totaling 3.5 million
pounds (our share) and purchases of 1.8 million pounds of uranium (purchased at an average unit cost of $83.78 per pound (US$60.15 per pound)) in the third quarter, our uranium inventory was 8.5 million pounds on September 30, 2026,
with an average inventory cost of $58.37 per pound. See Financial results by segment – Uranium in our third quarter MD&A for more information.

Contracting: In our uranium segment, over the next five years, we have contracts in place for average
annual deliveries of over 28 million pounds of U 3 O 8 per year, with commitments higher than the average in 2026 through 2028, and
lower than the average in 2029 and 2030. As the market continues to improve, we expect to continue layering in volumes that capture greater future upside using market-related pricing mechanisms.
2026 OUTLOOK UPDATE

Production : We have narrowed our guidance for our expected share of production of U 3 O 8 to be between 19.5 million and 20.5 million pounds (previously 19.5 million to 21.5 million pounds) for 2026,
reflecting greater certainty in the timing of uranium production as we approach the end of the year.

Sales/delivery volumes : We have narrowed our guidance for the sales/deliveries volumes in our uranium
segment to 29.5 to 30.5 million pounds (previously 29 to 32 million pounds) as we have greater confidence in the timing of potential uranium deliveries as we approach the end of the year.

Financial metrics: We have updated our guidance for average unit cost of sales, direct administration
costs and capital expenditures. See 2026 Outlook in our third quarter MD&A for more information.
ADDITIONAL HIGHLIGHTS

Westinghouse: In September, the US government, through the Department of Commerce, and the Republic of
Korea announced a non-binding framework that anticipates the investment by the Republic of Korea of up to US$120 billion to help finance the buildout of up to eight new large-scale reactors in the US,
including six Westinghouse AP1000 reactors. The framework builds upon the 2025 strategic partnership between Cameco, Brookfield and the US government and is subject to definitive agreements and other conditions.

In our 2026 second quarter MD&A, we updated the business framework for Westinghouse, replacing the framework
that was previously disclosed in our 2025 annual report. We have updated that business framework in our 2026 third quarter MD&A. See Our Operations - Westinghouse in our third quarter MD&A for more information

Changes to the executive team: consistent with prudent succession planning and with Cameco’s ongoing
commitment to execution of its balanced and disciplined strategy, effective January 1, 2027, the following changes will be made to the executive team:

Leah Hipperson will be appointed senior vice-president and chief financial officer, and

Heidi Shockey will assume the role of executive director, finance until March 31, 2027, at which time she
plans to retire.
With these changes in the senior leadership team, we expect to continue to have the right people in the
right positions, with the appropriate experience to help the company achieve its vision of powering a secure energy future.

Non-IFRS measures
The non-IFRS measures referenced in this document are supplemental measures, which are used as indicators of our
financial performance. Management believes that these non-IFRS measures provide useful supplemental information to investors, securities analysts, lenders and other interested parties in assessing our
operational performance and our ability to generate cash flows to meet our cash requirements. These measures are not recognized measures under IFRS, do not have standardized meanings, and are therefore unlikely to be comparable to similarly titled
measures presented by other companies. Accordingly, these measures should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for the financial information reported under IFRS. We are not able to reconcile our forward-looking non-IFRS guidance because we cannot predict the timing and amounts of discrete items, which could significantly impact our IFRS results.
The following are the non-IFRS measures used in this document.
ADJUSTED NET EARNINGS
Adjusted net earnings (ANE) is our
net earnings attributable to equity holders, adjusted for non-operating or non-cash items such as gains and losses on derivatives, unrealized foreign exchange gains and
losses, share-based compensation, adjustments to reclamation provisions flowing through other operating expenses, and bargain purchase gains, that we believe do not reflect the underlying financial performance for the reporting period. Other items
may also be adjusted from time to time. We adjust this measure for certain of the items that our equity-accounted investees make in arriving at other non-IFRS measures. Adjusted net earnings is one of the
targets that we measure to form the basis for a portion of annual employee and executive compensation (see Measuring our results in our 2025 annual MD&A).
In calculating ANE we adjust for derivatives. We do not use hedge accounting under IFRS and, therefore, we are required to report gains and losses on all
hedging activity, both for contracts that close in the period and those that remain outstanding at the end of the period. For the contracts that remain outstanding, we must treat them as though they were settled at the end of the reporting period (mark-to-market). However, we do not believe the gains and losses that we are required to report under IFRS appropriately reflect the intent of our hedging activities, so we
make adjustments in calculating our ANE to better reflect the impact of our hedging program in the applicable reporting period. See Foreign exchange in our 2025 annual MD&A for more information.
We also adjust for changes to our reclamation provisions that flow directly through earnings. Every quarter we are required to update the reclamation
provisions for all operations based on new cash flow estimates, discount and inflation rates. This
- 5 -
normally results in an adjustment to our asset retirement obligation asset in addition to the provision balance. When the assets of an operation have been written off due to an impairment, as is
the case with our Rabbit Lake and US ISR operations, the adjustment is recorded directly to the statement of earnings as “other operating expense (income)”. See note 10 of our interim financial statements for more information. This
amount has been excluded from our ANE measure.
The bargain purchase gain that was recognized when we acquired our
pro-rata share of Tokyo Electric Power Company Holding Inc’s (TEPCO) 5% participating interest in the Cigar Lake Joint Venture (CLJV) has also been removed in calculating ANE since it is non-cash, non-operating and outside of the normal course of our business. The gain was recorded in the statement of earnings as part of “other income (expense)”.
As a result of the change in ownership of Westinghouse when it was acquired by Cameco and Brookfield, Westinghouse’s inventories at the acquisition
date were revalued based on the market price at that date. As these quantities are sold, Westinghouse’s cost of products and services sold reflect these market values, regardless of their historic costs. Our share of these costs is included in
earnings from equity-accounted investees and recorded in cost of products and services sold in the investee information (see note 7 to the financial statements). Since this expense is outside of the normal course of business and only occurred due to
the change in ownership, we have excluded our share from our ANE measure.

EBITDA
EBITDA is defined
as net earnings attributable to equity holders, adjusted for the costs related to the impact of the company’s capital and tax structure including depreciation and amortization, finance income, finance costs (including accretion) and income
taxes.
ADJUSTED EBITDA
Adjusted EBITDA is defined
as EBITDA, as further adjusted for the impact of certain costs or benefits incurred in the period which are either not indicative of the underlying business performance or that impact the ability to assess the operating performance of the business.
These adjustments include the amounts noted in the ANE definition.
In calculating adjusted EBITDA, we also adjust for items included in the results of
our equity-accounted investees. These items are reported as part of marketing, administrative and general expenses within the investee financial information and are not representative of the underlying operations. These include gains/losses on
undesignated hedges, transaction costs related to acquisitions and gain/loss on disposition of a business.
The company may realize similar gains or incur
similar expenditures in the future.
ADJUSTED EBITDA MARGIN
Adjusted EBITDA margin is defined as adjusted EBITDA divided by revenue for the appropriate period.
EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA, and adjusted EBITDA margin are non-IFRS measures which allow us and other users to assess
results of operations from a management perspective without regard for our capital structure.

Profile
Cameco is one of the largest global providers of
the uranium fuel needed to power a secure energy future. Our competitive position is based on our controlling ownership of the world’s largest high-grade reserves and low-cost operations, as well as
significant investments across the nuclear fuel cycle, including ownership interests in Westinghouse Electric Company and Global Laser Enrichment. Utilities around the world rely on Cameco to provide global nuclear fuel solutions for the generation
of safe, reliable, carbon-free nuclear power. Our shares trade on the Toronto and New York stock exchanges. Our head office is in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, Canada.
As used in this news release, the terms we, us, our, the Company and Cameco mean Cameco Corporation and its subsidiaries unless otherwise indicated.
